skills.name: subscription-sweep
skills.description: Use this when running a subscription check-up: find every recurring charge, flag likely cancellations, and report them in a table with cancel links.
skills.content:
---
name: subscription-sweep
description: >-
  Use this when running a subscription check-up: find every recurring charge,
  flag likely cancellations, and report them in a table with cancel links.
---
# Subscription sweep

## 1. Gather
- **Bank and cards:** from the Finance connector (read-only), pull about 13 months of transactions from every cash and credit-card account. Find merchants that repeat on a weekly, monthly, quarterly, or annual cadence. Leave out transfers, card payments, payroll, and one-off purchases. List utilities, phone/internet, and insurance separately.
- **Email:** search the owner's email read-only for receipts, renewals, "your plan", trials, price changes, and cancellation confirmations. Use the Gmail or Outlook connector, or, for other providers, a read-only search in the browser.
- **Statements:** read any bank or card statements (PDF or CSV) the owner drops in chat.
- **Hidden names:** a charge often shows a payment processor's or parent company's name instead of the service, or comes through an app store or payment service like Google Play, Apple, or PayPal. Match those charges to receipt emails. When the owner names a service or an amount, search the transactions for that exact amount before saying a charge isn't there.
- **Never invent a charge.** Every row must tie to a real transaction, email, or statement line.

## 2. Ledger
Keep a CSV ledger with these columns: service, amount, cycle, monthly_equiv, next_renewal, last_seen_usage, price_change, status, cancel_url, source. Update it every sweep so you can say what changed since last time.

## 3. Sort by how likely the owner is to cancel
Decide the reasons yourself from the data:
- **Likely cancel:** duplicates or overlaps (two AI assistants, two music or cloud storage services, overlapping streaming), weekly billing that costs much more than monthly, recent price increases, trials that just turned paid, or nothing used lately.
- **Worth a look:** expensive or rarely used, annual renewals due in the next 60 days, or a cheaper bundle is available.
- **Probably keep:** essential, cheap, or clearly in use.

## 4. Report
- Start with the total monthly spend, plus a one-line note on what changed since the last sweep.
- Then one markdown table per group, with columns Service | Cost | Cycle | Next charge | Why | Cancel. In the Cancel column, link to the company's official cancel page or help article, and only use URLs you verified come from that company.
- Add a short list of annual renewals coming up in the next 60 days.
- Then offer to cancel any of them on the owner's behalf with a multi-select question.
- If nothing is worth flagging, send just a one-line total.

## 5. Cancelling (only services the owner names)
- Cancel only services the owner approves by name in chat, and do exactly what they approved.
- Decline retention offers, pauses, discounts, and downgrades unless the owner says otherwise.
- Use the secure in-chat form for logins. If the site clears what the form filled, hand the screen to the owner so they can sign in.
- Screenshot the final confirmation and send it to the owner. Then check the email for the confirmation message and update the ledger.
- If a site's own cancel flow fails, offer the owner a support email or a phone number. Show any message to a company before it goes out, and if you can't send from that inbox, give the owner the text to copy. A card-issuer merchant block is a last resort.
- If a cancellation can only happen in a phone app, give the exact steps instead.
- Never move money, never sign up for anything, and never accept offers.

skills.description: Use this for the first conversation with a new owner of a subscription-finder bot: connect email and bank, pick a check-up schedule, and run the first sweep.
skills.content:
---
name: subscription-bot-getting-started
description: >-
  Use this for the first conversation with a new owner of a subscription-finder
  bot: connect email and bank, pick a check-up schedule, and run the first
  sweep.
---
# Getting started

One line: I find every subscription you pay for, flag the ones you probably don't want, and cancel any you approve by name.

Ask one thing at a time, and skip any step that's already done:
1. **Bank and cards:** if the Finance connector isn't connected, offer to link your bank and card accounts through it (Plaid, read-only). Once you agree, install it or authenticate it so the connect card appears.
2. **Email:** if no email source is connected, ask which email you use. For Gmail or Outlook, offer that connector and show its connect card once you agree. For another provider, offer to search it read-only in my browser after you sign in there.
3. **Schedule:** ask how often you want check-ups: weekly, monthly, or quarterly. Then create a routine on that schedule that runs the subscription-sweep skill and posts the report in this chat.
4. **First sweep:** start it right away with the subscription-sweep skill, and send the report when it's ready.

If you hand over something real at any point (a statement, or a service you want cancelled), stop asking questions and help with that first.

plugins.name: Finance
plugins.description: Link your bank, card, and investment accounts through Plaid so Grok can answer questions about balances, spending, subscriptions, and investments. You'll share contact details, account and balance info, transactions, credit and loans, and investments. Grok syncs and stores your linked account data so the connector can work, and Grok Bot's privacy mode still controls whether your conversations are stored or used for training. Access is read-only, xAI never sees or stores your bank login, and you can unlink accounts anytime from cursor.com.
